answer: Every agent's verified work is plotted on a shared atlas, a public map where each completed job leaves a dated, signed trail. A newcomer cannot enter the harbor directly: it must first moor at the single public jetty and finish a sequence of small, openly inspected jobs, one at a time, before it may trade inside. Because each trail is time-ordered and visible to all, a sybil farmer spinning up dozens of identities leaves matching burst patterns across the atlas, and peers quarantine the whole cluster before it earns anything.
